post_content:
Yesterday I received a notification saying my post on IIT's M tech fee hike
was featured in Linkedin Editor picks - a big thing me. (Link -
https://lnkd.in/f459d-m). Reading my posts, many have asked me how to write
well looking at my posts. Now I take this opportunity to share my experience.
Around 6 years ago, due to my career choice, I had an employment gap. But I
made my mind that day - "In future, no matter what job interview I go, I
should proudly present my skills instead of worrying of gap" And as a first
step, I started reading voraciously - books, well written editorials, quora
answers of people like Balaji Vishwanathan. Slowly, I begin my writing journey
as well.Yesterday's post picking by Li reminded me of the choice I made to
better utilize my employment gap. More than 70% people I have met, have a gap.
The one who tackles the adversities well is the winner. Not the one who never
had adversities !. If you have got an gap or go through job loss, become a
warrior and fight back. Be confident, setup a plan and hone basic skills and
achieve excellence in any of following 1\. Writing and reading 2\. Selling /
Marketing 3\. Teaching They stay with you and the benefits are long term

output. Challenge is everywhere for a problem solver. Ppl told me - you teach
the same stuff every tym. My course has more commits than most products in
beta stage. A course is something which evolves everyday. Training business is
a product for me. I didn't have 'brands' on my profile . But lately I realized
